groups.label: Hyperscalers
groups.reading: Compute sold alongside storage, networking and everything else. You pay more per GPU-hour than anywhere below, and you get the contracts, the compliance paperwork and the regions that an enterprise procurement team asks for.

providers.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
providers.summary: Hyperscaler offering bare-metal NVIDIA clusters and RDMA superclusters, a named supplier to several frontier AI labs.

groups.label: Specialist GPU clouds
groups.reading: Companies whose whole business is renting accelerators. Dedicated capacity, reserved instances, and the interconnect that multi-node training needs. This is where most serious training work goes.

providers.name: CoreWeave
providers.summary: GPU-specialised cloud operating its own data centers, one of the largest dedicated AI compute providers.

providers.name: Crusoe
providers.summary: AI cloud that sites compute next to stranded and low-carbon energy, selling clusters and managed inference.

providers.name: FluidStack
providers.summary: Enterprise GPU cloud that provisions dedicated clusters across a network of partner data centers rather than owning the halls.

providers.name: Lambda
providers.summary: GPU cloud and on-premise systems vendor selling on-demand instances, reserved clusters and workstations.

providers.name: Nebius
providers.summary: AI-focused cloud operating its own data centers in Europe and the US, spun out of the former Yandex group.

providers.name: Paperspace
providers.summary: Developer-facing GPU virtual machines and managed ML environments, acquired by DigitalOcean.

providers.name: RunPod
providers.summary: On-demand and spot GPU instances plus serverless GPU endpoints aimed at individual developers and small teams.

providers.name: Together AI
providers.summary: GPU cloud for training, fine-tuning and inference of open-source models, sold as both clusters and a serverless inference API.

groups.label: Marketplaces
groups.reading: Other people's idle machines, resold by the hour. The cheapest compute you will find, with the weakest guarantees: a host can reclaim a machine, and hardware varies between listings. Good for experiments, poor for a run you cannot restart.

providers.name: Vast.ai
providers.summary: Peer-to-peer marketplace where third-party hosts rent out GPU capacity, priced by bid against host-set rates rather than a published rate card.

groups.label: Decentralised networks
groups.reading: Capacity coordinated by a protocol rather than a company, usually settled in a token. Prices can be very low and availability is uneven. Read the terms carefully, because there is no single counterparty to hold to them.

providers.name: Akash Network
providers.summary: Open-source decentralized compute marketplace where providers bid to host workloads, settled on-chain.

providers.name: io.net
providers.summary: Decentralized GPU network aggregating capacity from data centers, independent operators and individual owners into clusters.
